correctness.rationale: Reconstructed equation (3.21) from the primary numerator, including normalization Q=s^(1-2n)P(s,s). For m=2n+1, parity gives L(2r)=L(2r+1)=r+1, kappa(2r)=n-1-r and kappa(2r+1)=2n-1-r. Summing yields endpoints n, a_j=(8n-4)j+2 for 1<=j<=n, center 8n^2+4n+1 and reciprocal degree 2(n+1). The centered circle polynomial is (8n-4)|sum_{j=0}^n exp(ij theta)|^2+5+4 sum_{j=1}^n cos(j theta)+2n cos((n+1)theta). With u=theta/2, v=(n+1)theta, H=(4n-2)/sin^2(u)-(2n-2)>=2n/sin^2(u), completion of the square gives T>=2n+1-(1-sin^2(u))/n>=2n+1-1/n>0. theta=0 is checked directly; theta=2pi/(n+1) gives T=2n+1. Nonzero endpoints and reciprocal pairing give exactly n+1 roots on each side of the unit circle, with multiplicity. An interior root s realizes product coordinates (s,s) by choosing both z coordinates sqrt(|s|) exp(i arg s), both w coordinates sqrt(|s|); both points lie in the domain since m/n>1. The denominator is nonzero. This is not the kernel diagonal z=w. Separately authored exact coefficient comparisons for n=1,...,500 corroborate, but do not replace, the uniform parity and inequality proof.
